title: A normal-mean interval with known spread

source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
aliases: a normal-mean interval with known spread
purpose: How precisely does an observed mean locate the unknown mean cutting error?
meaning: Divide the known population standard deviation by the square root of the whole-number sample size. Multiply that standard error by the standard normal 0.975 quantile, then place the resulting margin of error on each side of the observed mean.

definition.setting: A calibration workshop summarizes independent, identically normally distributed cutting errors by an observed mean x̄. Assume the population standard deviation σ is known. Choose a whole number n of readings and watch the interval narrow around that same entered mean. No new readings are invented as n changes.

signature.x̄: Observed sample mean error, in millimetres
signature.σ: Known positive population standard deviation, in millimetres
signature.SE: Standard error of the sample mean, in millimetres
signature.h: Margin on each side of the observed mean, in millimetres
signature.I: Computed interval of candidate population mean values
signature.μ: Fixed unknown population mean, not a plotted known value
signature.Φ⁻¹: Quantile function of the standard normal distribution

conditions: Independent, identically normal readings with one common unknown mean μ and known positive population spread σ are assumptions, not conclusions from these controls. Use n from 1 to 64, x̄ from −4 to 4 mm and σ from 0.25 to 2 mm. The ideal repeated-sampling procedure covers fixed μ with probability 0.95. One computed interval has fixed endpoints; this is not a 95% posterior probability for μ or an interval predicting the next reading. An estimated spread requires a different procedure. The quantile is numerical, z₀.₉₇₅≈1.959963984540054; 1.96 is only its rounded display.
